sportsdataverse.lacrosse — 19 endpoints. Note: Runtime only: each call sends one GET to stats.premierlacrosseleague.com/api, the proxy behind the Premier Lacrosse League's own stats site. sdv-py publishes no release assets from this API and ships no bulk or backfill tooling for it. Requests from one process are spaced at least half a second apart. Note: No token: the stats routes need no key and the site keeps its upstream key server-side. The proxy answers only requests carrying the stats site's own Referer (the runtime sends it); without it the answer is HTTP 403 "Origin not allowed" (AssetFetchError). No environment variable is read. Note: Seasons 2019 to 2026 (year). The per-game wrappers (game, play-by-play, box scores, insights) work from 2021: the 2019 and 2020 game slugs contain "@" and the proxy refuses them (NoDataError). Note: Ids are strings. Per-game wrappers take event_slug (from pll_schedule; the slug format changes by season, so read it, never build it), team wrappers team_slug (from pll_team_season_stats, e.g. waterdogs, boston-cannons) and player wrappers player_slug (from pll_player_season_stats). Team codes (WAT) and six-digit player ids are columns, not route keys. Note: ESPN: espn_lacrosse_* (league pll) already carries PLL scoreboards, schedules, standings and team pages, but ESPN's PLL summary has no play-by-play and empty box scores; these wrappers add play-by-play, box scores, season and advanced stats, leaders, rosters and bios. The two share no game id: join on the UTC start time and the team codes (ESPN's abbreviations equal team_id here).
